newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Q1 GDP rise 5.1 pct - Finance Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Q1 GDP rise 5.1 pct - Finance Ministry.

text.p: Mexico's gross domestic product (GDP) rose 5.1 percent in the first quarter compared with the same quarter a year earlier, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
It said that adjusted for the effect of having fewer working days in the first quarter of this year compared with the same quarter a year earlier GDP rose by just over 6.0 percent.
A survey of 10 brokerage houses and research firms in Mexico City by Reuters forecasted a rise in GDP of 5.12 percent.
"With this rise, GDP has grown for four consecutive quarters," the Finance Ministry said.
The ministry said the industrial sector led growth with a 6.2 percent gain in the quarter.
Within that sector, construction rose 8.7 percent, followed by manufacturing, up 6.2 percent.
Output of electricity, gas and water rose 5.4 percent, while mining production was up 1.0 percent, it said.
Growth in the overall services sector was up 5.0 percent, it said.
Within the services sector, commerce, restaurants and hotels grew 5.6 percent in the first quarter, after falling more than 6.0 percent in the same quarter a year earlier.
The Ministry said the rise in services was mostly fueled by an increase in spending on investment and intermediate goods, while output of final consumer goods during the quarter showed a decline.
Transportation, storage, and communications rose 7.3 percent, it said.
Financial services, insurance, and real estate rose 4.7 percent in the quarter, with the most significant growth in financial services.
Community, social and personal services rose 3.6 percent over the year, it said.
Agriculture, fishing, and forestry rose 1.6 percent in the quarter over the year.
The Ministry said that in the first quarter of this year there were 71 working days, compared to 75 working days in the first quarter of last year.
